text:
Marathon Petroleum stock jumped 3.95% today, adding to a sharp 21.7% climb over two weeks. The immediate driver appears to be oil price strength—world crude is trading at $125.44 per barrel, well above US prices at $96.24, and refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, near full utilization. Reports of geopolitical tensions (Iran fortifying nuclear sites, Saudi airport attack, Saudi-Houthi conflict) and supply uncertainty around Russian diesel are keeping crude elevated and supporting refiner margins, since higher oil prices boost the value of refined products relative to crude costs.

The broader picture is that a refiner benefits when global oil prices stay elevated and regional supply gets tight—even as political pressure mounts to bring fuel prices down. With elections weeks away and Trump negotiating Russian diesel imports, there's real uncertainty about future supply, which keeps the market pricing in scarcity premiums that work in refiners' favor right now.
